# Evaluating ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Integration by Parts (Applied Twice)

Let **I = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx**

**First application of integration by parts:**

Let u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
Then du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cos(x) + \int \text{exp}(x)\sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second application of integration by parts** on the remaining integral:

Let u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
Then du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \text{exp}(x)\sin(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\sin(x) - \int \text{exp}(x)\cos(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\sin(x) - I$$

## Combining

Substituting back:

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\sin(x) - I$$

$$2I = \text{exp}(x)\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{\text{exp}(x)(\sin(x) + \cos(x))}{2} + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:

$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{\text{exp}(x)(\sin(x)+\cos(x))}{2}\right] = \frac{\text{exp}(x)(\sin(x)+\cos(x)) + \text{exp}(x)(\cos(x)-\sin(x))}{2} = \text{exp}(x)\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x))/2 + C</answer>

I need to evaluate the indefinite integral ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx.

This is a classic integral that requires integration by parts twice, or I can use the known formula.

Let me use integration by parts. Let:
I = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

First integration by parts:
Let u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
Then du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

I = exp(x)*cos(x) - ∫ exp(x)*(-sin(x)) dx
I = exp(x)*cos(x) + ∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx

Now for the second integral, integration by parts again:
Let u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
Then du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - I

So:
I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - I
2I = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)
I = exp(x)*cos(x)/2 + exp(x)*sin(x)/2 + C
I = exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2 + C

Let me verify by differentiating:
d/dx [exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2]
= exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))/2 + exp(x)*(-sin(x) + cos(x))/2
= exp(x)*[cos(x) + sin(x) - sin(x) + cos(x)]/2
= exp(x)*[2*cos(x)]/2
= exp(x)*cos(x) ✓

So the answer is exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x))/2 + C
